record.paper_title: On free curves and related open problems
record.context_brief: Existence of odd-degree maximizing ADE curves
record.original_question: For every odd degree d=2m+1 ≥ 5, does there exist a maximizing plane curve C in P^2 with only simple ADE singularities and total Tjurina number τ(C)=3m^2+1? Equivalently, do maximizing odd-degree curves C_{2m+1} exist in every such degree?

evidence.quote: A reduced curve C in P2 with only A, D, E singularities and of odd degree d = 2m + 1 ≥ 5 is a maximizing curve if τ (C) = 3m2 + 1.
Question 7.5. Do maximizing curves C2m+1 exist in any degree d = 2m + 1 ≥ 5 ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work in the complex projective plane $\mathbb{P}^2$. A reduced plane curve $C\subset\mathbb{P}^2$ is said to have only simple (ADE) singularities if each of its singular points is analytically equivalent to one of the singularities of type $A_k$ ($k\ge 1$), $D_k$ ($k\ge 4$), $E_6$, $E_7$, or $E_8$. For a reduced plane curve $C$ of degree $d$, the total Tjurina number is
$$\tau(C)=\sum_{p\in\mathrm{Sing}(C)}\dim_{\mathbb{C}}\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^2,p}/(f,\partial_x f,\partial_y f),$$
where $f$ is a local equation of $C$ at $p$.

A reduced curve $C\subset\mathbb{P}^2$ of odd degree $d=2m+1\ge 5$ having only ADE singularities is called a maximizing curve if
$$\tau(C)=3m^2+1.$$

Question: For every odd integer $d=2m+1\ge 5$, does there exist a maximizing plane curve $C_{2m+1}\subset\mathbb{P}^2$ in degree $d$ (i.e. a reduced curve with only ADE singularities and total Tjurina number $3m^2+1$)?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears to remain open in general. Recent work (2024) provides only non-existence criteria and partial results: maximizing curves of degree 7 have been studied, but no examples of maximizing odd-degree curves of degree ≥ 11 are known, and no construction settling existence for all odd d=2m+1≥5 has been published.

status_evidence.claim: Recent work gives only non-existence criteria, not a general existence construction.
